info.title: OpenAsy Infrastructure API
info.summary: Hosts, containers and Kubernetes, read without installing anything, with every change kept.
info.description:
Every screen of Infrastructure uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Hosts are read over SSH as an unprivileged `openasy` account with 5-minute certificates, and clusters through their API with a read-only token (ADR 0031). Each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`). Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

get.description:
The OpenAsy products of this install and their addresses, from `OPENASY_PRODUCTS`, for the product switcher. Empty when it is not set.

Needs the viewer role.

200.description: The products, in the order they are configured.

get.description:
What to put on hosts comes from each agent: GET /api/v1/agents/{id}/setup.

Needs the viewer role.

post.description:
Returns a one-time enrolment token, valid for 7 days. Start infra-agent with it; the agent then has its own secret (ADR 0023).

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
Only an agent that reads no hosts. Its secret stops working.

Needs the admin role.

post.description:
A new one-time token, for an agent that lost its volume or whose CA changed. Its old secret stops working; its hosts must trust the new CA.

Needs the admin role.

get.summary: What to put on the hosts this agent reads
get.description:
Its CA public key, the sshd drop-in, the sudoers file that matches its script, the commands to prepare a host and the fixed key.

Needs the viewer role.

post.summary: infra-agent: enrol with a one-time token
post.description: Called by infra-agent, not by people. Returns the agent's own secret for every later call.
Called by infra-agent with its secret every few seconds. Each job is leased for 10 minutes. Answers 409 when the agent's version differs from infra's (ADR 0019).

post.summary: infra-agent: send what a job found
post.description: Facts are parsed and masked by the agent; Infrastructure checks their shape and stores what changed. Gzip the body.

Infrastructure asks the host for its key right away. Check the fingerprint on the host and accept it before the first collection.

Needs the admin role.

patch.description:
A new address or port unpins the host key.

Needs the admin role.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` on plain http://localhost).

apiToken.description: An API token from Settings → API tokens (`oa_infra_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

unreadable.description: What needs the sudo rules or the container switch to be read.

source.description: file: from the hosts file (OPENASY_HOSTS, ADR 0052); changed there, so PATCH and DELETE answer 409. Fetching its key still works.

fileHostKey.description: The fingerprint hostKey gives in the hosts file: a host that presents that key is trusted without an admin, and no other key can be accepted here.

containers.description: Read containers through the host's Docker or Podman. Access to the socket is equivalent to root (ADR 0031).

hostKeys.description: Pinned. Collection stops when the host presents another key.

pendingHostKeys.description: What the host presents now, waiting to be checked and accepted.

status.description: Of the last collection. new and host-key-pending wait for an admin to accept the host key.

agentId.description: The agent that reads this host. Optional when there is only one.

auth.description: certificate: a 5-minute certificate from Infrastructure's CA for each collection. key: one fixed key in authorized_keys.

jumpHostId.description: Reach the host through this one (ProxyJump).

Facts.description: Everything read from the host in one collection. Values that look like secrets are masked; container environment variables are names only.

envNames.description: Names only: values are never collected.

caCert.description: The cluster CA in PEM; null to use the system's.

token.description: Token of the read-only service account from GET /api/v1/setup. Stored encrypted, never returned.

ClusterFacts.description: Nodes, namespaces, workloads, pods, services, ingresses, volumes, cluster-admin bindings and recent warnings.

caFingerprint.description: Of the SSH certificate authority the agent made; hosts read by it trust this CA.

enrollToken.description: One-time; start infra-agent with INFRA_ENROLL_TOKEN set to it. Shown once.

AgentReport.description: What infra-agent says about itself on every call: its version (it must equal infra's, ADR 0019), its public keys, and the host setup that matches its script.

Result.description: One of: facts (a collection), hostKeys (the keys a host presents), or error.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

hostsFile.description: null when OPENASY_HOSTS is not set.

appliedAt.description: When it was last read and applied; null if it never was.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied.

warnings.description: What to fix that did not stop the file from being applied, such as a host whose agent is not enrolled yet.

HostsFile.description: The hosts file (ADR 0052), shared with Logs. It is read again within a minute of a change; a file that cannot be applied leaves the hosts from its last good version.
